name: Podcast mic and EQ boost

card.summary: Close-miking and low-end EQ make a recording sound deeper; the speaker's actual voice is unchanged.
card.note: Affects recordings only, not the live voice.

quick.overview:
This is audio processing aimed at making a recorded voice sound deeper. A directional microphone used close to the mouth naturally boosts bass, and EQ can add more.

No studies have examined it as an appearance or social-perception tool.
quick.mechanism: The proximity effect raises low frequencies when a speaker is near a directional microphone; EQ further adjusts frequency balance.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented. The effect exists only in the recording or broadcast.

lead: A podcast microphone with an equalizer (EQ) boost is a recording setup in which a directional microphone is used close to the mouth and low frequencies are raised electronically, so that a recorded voice sounds deeper, warmer and fuller. It is discussed in voice-focused corners of appearance and self-improvement culture as a way to make a recorded voice, such as on a podcast, video or call, sound more resonant and authoritative.

Part of the effect is acoustic. Directional microphones such as cardioids boost bass when the sound source is very close, a phenomenon called the proximity effect, which makes voices sound warmer and fuller and which radio announcers are often said to use for an authoritative tone [1]. Equalization is the separate, electronic adjustment of frequency balance, including low-shelf controls that raise or lower everything below a chosen frequency [2]. The change affects only the recording or broadcast, not the speaker's own voice.

The interest in a deeper-sounding voice follows research on voice perception. In one study, men's voices were rated most attractive when pitched about 25 Hz lower than the original recordings, with a peak near 96 Hz, while dominance ratings kept rising as pitch fell [3].

chain: Directional mic used close to the mouth
Proximity effect and low-shelf EQ raise bass
Recorded voice sounds deeper and fuller
angle.text: Close-miking and low-end EQ change how a voice sounds in recordings and streams, giving it more bass weight. The speaker's unprocessed voice stays the same.

infobox: Proximity effect (bass boost at close range) [1]

paras: In directional microphones, sound reaches both sides of the diaphragm, and at very short distances the pressure difference favors low frequencies, tilting the response toward bass. Omnidirectional microphones generally do not show the effect. Engineers who find the boost unwanted may change microphone type or working distance [1].

Equalization adjusts the level of frequency bands. A low shelf raises or lowers frequencies below a set point, with a gradual transition of at most about 6 dB per octave, and such broad adjustments mainly make sound more pleasing to the listener [2]. Wikipedia notes that room acoustics can make response uneven, that boosting near a feedback frequency can cause howling, and that EQ changes phase, which some listeners hear as a change in timbre [2].

A 2016 Behavioral Ecology study that manipulated recordings found men's voices most attractive when pitched moderately lower than the original, around 96 Hz against an average adult male speaking pitch of roughly 120 Hz; voices pitched lower than that were rated less attractive, while perceived dominance rose steadily as pitch dropped [3]. The study altered pitch, whereas a mic and EQ change timbre and bass emphasis, so it does not test this setup directly.
No studies found on podcast microphones or EQ boosts as appearance or social-perception tools. Related research on how listeners rate pitch-shifted voices is described above [3].
